literal.prompt: Как назывался документ, которым Верховный тайный совет пытался ограничить власть Анны Иоанновны?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The official library article identifies Anna's accession in January 1730 (L52) and says the Council proposed the Conditions to create limited monarchy, preventing independent war/peace decisions, appointments, and tax changes (L53). It states she publicly tore them in Moscow (L54); this directly grounds the prompt and unique key. The other three labels are separate real Russian historical texts: the 1551 council decision collection (Stoglav, L48), the 1497 unified legislative code (Sudebnik, L58), and the 1785 city self-government charter (city page L44, L48-L50). Those are plausible document-category alternatives, but their own dates and functions do not satisfy the 1730 Anna relation.
literalGroups.locator: President Library, full returned page L52-L54; especially L53-L54.; President Library, full returned page L44-L64; especially L48.; President Library, full returned page L44-L63; especially L58.; President Library, full returned page L40-L55; especially L44 and L48-L51.

literalGroups.literal: «Кондиции» 1730 года лишали Анну Иоанновну возможности самостоятельно заключать мир и объявлять войну. Прибыв в Москву, она публично разорвала их, опираясь на поддержку среднего и мелкого дворянства и гвардии.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The first sentence states that the Conditions removed Anna's independent ability to make peace or declare war (official library L53). The second states that she publicly tore them in Moscow and relied on support from the middle/lower nobility and Guards (L54). Both are directly supported by the same complete page.
literalGroups.locator: President Library, full returned page L52-L54; especially L53-L54.

literalGroups.literal: Стоглав — сборник решений церковного собора 1551 года.
literalGroups.primaryGround: Stoglav is the collection of decisions of the 1551 church council; the library says those decisions regulated church life and religious rites (L48). This is a concrete fact about this option, not a generic category label.
literalGroups.locator: President Library, full returned page L44-L64; especially L48.

literalGroups.literal: «Кондиции» ограничивали самостоятельное назначение Анной Иоанновной чиновников и изменение налогов.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The 1497 Sudebnik is described as a unified legislative code reflecting prior legal sources and introduced to meet the need for a unified legal system (L58). This teaches what this distractor did, beyond its title.
literalGroups.locator: President Library, full returned page L44-L63; especially L58.

literalGroups.literal: Судебник 1497 года унифицировал нормы права Московского государства.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The city page dates Catherine II's signature to 1785 (L44), names the City Charter (L48), and says it established elected urban institutions and foundations of self-government (L50). This is a concrete fact about this distractor.
literalGroups.locator: President Library, full returned page L40-L55; especially L44 and L48-L51.

literalGroups.literal: Жалованная грамота городам 1785 года определила устройство городского самоуправления.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Conditions also prevented Anna from independently appointing state officials and changing the tax system (official library L53). This is an additional, useful own-option fact beyond the prompt/key and is distinct from the war/peace detail in the explanation.
literalGroups.locator: President Library, full returned page L52-L54; especially L53-L54.

absoluteDifficulty.audienceGround: An adult who regularly studies Russian history or the 18th-century succession may recall the Conditions, but the exact name is a specific 1730 political-history detail. A general adult without that knowledge must identify one title among four real Russian historical documents; the distractors are parallel in broad type and are not absurd.
absoluteDifficulty.judgment: This is an absolute-level editorial judgment under the project criteria: the exact source/event must be known, rather than inferred from wording alone. The answer set allows some chronology-based narrowing, but does not turn the question into broad adult knowledge or an arbitrary four-name guess.
